official_api.name: AT Protocol XRPC API (com.atproto.* on the user's PDS, app.bsky.* lexicons; video via video.bsky.app)
official_api.docs_url: https://atproto.com/specs/oauth (OAuth spec); https://github.com/bluesky-social/bsky-docs (docs source; docs.bsky.app now 308-redirects to bsky.network/docs and endpoints.bsky.app); https://github.com/bluesky-social/atproto/tree/main/lexicons (authoritative schemas)
official_api.auth:
Two routes, both free, no developer registration, no app review.

(A) Legacy app-password session (verified, still works, officially 'acceptable for bots and command line tools'; 'Applications with an end user login flow should use OAuth' per atproto.com/guides/sdk-auth). User creates an app password at https://bsky.app/settings/app-passwords (format xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx; optional 'privileged' toggle for DM access - leave off). App: POST {PDS}/xrpc/com.atproto.server.createSession {identifier: handle-or-email-or-DID, password: app-password} -> {accessJwt, refreshJwt, did, handle, didDoc, email?, emailConfirmed?, active?, status?}. Use `Authorization: Bearer <accessJwt>`; when it expires POST {PDS}/xrpc/com.atproto.server.refreshSession with `Authorization: Bearer <refreshJwt>` (returns a new pair). Errors: AccountTakedown, AuthFactorTokenRequired (email 2FA; retry with authFactorToken). PDS = https://bsky.social for Bluesky-hosted accounts, otherwise resolve via DID doc (see below). Limits: createSession 30 per 5 min and 300/day per account.

(B) AT Protocol OAuth 2.1 profile (verified from https://atproto.com/specs/oauth, read 2026-10-07). Mandatory for ALL client types: PKCE S256 ('plain' forbidden), PAR (pushed authorization requests), DPoP-bound tokens with ES256 keys and server nonces, client metadata document. There is no client registration: the `client_id` IS the https URL of a JSON client-metadata document the app publishes anywhere on the public web (static hosting such as GitHub Pages is fine; must be served 200 with Content-Type application/json, no redirects). Required fields: client_id, application_type ('native' for NEFORUM), grant_types ['authorization_code','refresh_token'], response_types ['code'], redirect_uris, scope (must include 'atproto'), dpop_bound_access_tokens true, token_endpoint_auth_method 'none' (public client). Native clients: redirect_uri may be a custom scheme that 'must match the client_id hostname in reverse-domain order' (client_id host app.example.com -> `com.example.app:/callback`, note single slash), or an https URL on the same origin as client_id (App Links / Universal Links). A hosted-https client_id may NOT use http://127.0.0.1 loopback; loopback exists only via the special 'localhost client': client_id = `http://localhost` (literal, no port) with virtual metadata in query params, e.g. `http://localhost?redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%2Fcallback&scope=atproto%20repo%3Aapp.bsky.feed.post` ; redirect to http://127.0.0.1/<path> or http://[::1]/<path> where 'Path components must match, but port numbers are not matched' (so bind any free port); hostname 'localhost' itself is NOT allowed in redirect URIs. Official Go/Node CLI tutorials use exactly this loopback client but state 'This is for local development. The loopback client won't work in production' (it does function against bsky.social today; treat as unofficial for shipping). Public (no-backend) clients: access tokens < 30 min (5-15 min typical), refresh tokens rotate on every use (single-use), whole session capped at 2 weeks -> user must re-authorize every 14 days; confidential clients (needs a server holding a private key) get up to 180 days - not possible for a local-first app. Flow: resolve handle->DID->PDS (DID doc service #atproto_pds) -> GET {PDS}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource -> authorization_servers[0] -> GET {AS}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server -> POST PAR endpoint (with code_challenge, dpop proof, scope, login_hint) -> open authorize URL in system browser -> callback -> POST token endpoint with DPoP -> verify `sub` DID equals the DID resolved at start -> call PDS with `Authorization: DPoP <token>` plus a fresh DPoP proof header on every request. Flutter: pub.dev packages `atproto` 2.5.0 (BSD-3, createSession + OAuthSessionManager with automatic DPoP/refresh) and `atproto_oauth` 0.8.3 (Android/iOS/Linux/macOS/Windows; uses flutter_web_auth_2 with a custom scheme; store sessions incl. DPoP private key in flutter_secure_storage). Bluesky's own `@atproto/oauth-client-expo` README example: redirect_uris ['com.example:/auth/callback'], application_type 'native'.
oauth_scopes: transition:generic (legacy broad PDS write/blob/preferences scope; still accepted, being replaced by granular scopes)
repo:app.bsky.feed.post?action=create (granular: create posts only; omit ?action for create+update+delete)

rpc:<lxm>?aud=<DID> (granular: service-auth / proxied calls; e.g. rpc:*?aud=did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview as in Bluesky's expo example; needed for getServiceAuth used by video upload - exact string for video unverified)
include:<nsid> (permission sets bundled by a lexicon namespace)

endpoints.notes: Protocol-level alternatives: DNS TXT at _atproto.{handle} with value `did=did:...` (preferred on conflict) or GET https://{handle}/.well-known/atproto-did (text/plain body = DID). Also used to build mention facets.

endpoints.purpose: Resolve DID to DID document -> PDS URL
endpoints.response_shape: DID doc; find service[] entry with id ending '#atproto_pds', type 'AtprotoPersonalDataServer', use serviceEndpoint (https URL of the PDS)
endpoints.notes: Verify handle bidirectionally (DID doc alsoKnownAs contains at://{handle}). Cache < 10 min during auth flows.

endpoints.response_shape: {authorization_servers:[...]} then AS metadata (pushed_authorization_request_endpoint, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, require_pushed_authorization_requests:true, scopes_supported)
{accessJwt, refreshJwt, handle, did, didDoc?, email?, emailConfirmed?, emailAuthFactor?, active?, status?('takendown'|'suspended'|'deactivated')}
endpoints.notes: Errors: AccountTakedown, AuthFactorTokenRequired. Rate limit 30/5min and 300/day per account.
Refresh JWTs rotate; persist the new pair.

endpoints.request_shape: Headers: Authorization (Bearer accessJwt or DPoP token), Content-Type: image/jpeg|image/png|image/webp|... ; body = raw bytes (lexicon input encoding */*)
endpoints.notes: Blob 'will be deleted if it is not referenced within a time window (eg, minutes)' - create the post record promptly. Post images: accept image/*, maxSize 2,000,000 bytes each (lexicon app.bsky.embed.images, raised from 1,000,000 in 2026), max 4 per post. Link-card thumb: maxSize 1,000,000 bytes. Client should downscale/re-encode (the official app re-encodes to JPEG and strips EXIF).

endpoints.purpose: Create a post (also replies, quotes, link cards, media posts)
endpoints.notes: CREATE costs 3 rate-limit points. For a thread: post 1 has no reply; post N has reply.root = post 1 {uri,cid} and reply.parent = post N-1 {uri,cid} taken from each createRecord response. Images embed: {"$type":"app.bsky.embed.images","images":[{"alt":"...","image":<blob>,"aspectRatio":{"width":w,"height":h}}]}. Link card: {"$type":"app.bsky.embed.external","external":{"uri":"https://...","title":"...","description":"...","thumb"?:<blob<=1MB>}}. Video: {"$type":"app.bsky.embed.video","video":<blob from video service>,"aspectRatio":{...},"alt"?:"...","captions"?:[{lang,file<=20000B text/vtt}] (max 20)}. Quote: {"$type":"app.bsky.embed.record","record":{uri,cid}}; quote+media: app.bsky.embed.recordWithMedia. Only ONE embed per post (images OR link card OR video). Error InvalidSwap only if swapCommit used. Web URL of the result: https://bsky.app/profile/{handle-or-did}/post/{rkey} where rkey is the last path segment of uri.

endpoints.purpose: Mint service-auth token for the video service
endpoints.url: {PDS}/xrpc/com.atproto.server.getServiceAuth?aud=did:web:{PDS host, e.g. did:web:bsky.social or the user's entryway host}&lxm=com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob&exp={unix seconds, now+1800}
endpoints.notes: Per official video tutorial the aud is the PDS DID (did:web:<pds host>), NOT did:web:video.bsky.app; lxm is com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob. Requires the user's PDS session; under granular OAuth scopes you need a matching rpc: scope (exact string unverified).

endpoints.request_shape: Headers: Authorization: Bearer <service-auth token>, Content-Type: video/mp4, Content-Length: <bytes>; body = raw video bytes
endpoints.notes: Lexicon embed accepts video/mp4 only, maxSize 300,000,000 bytes (300 MB); Bluesky announced 10-minute / 300 MB limit on 2026-08-25/26 (was 60 s in Sept 2024, 3 min from Jan 2026). Daily quota per Sept-2024 launch post: 25 videos or 10 GB per day ('we may tweak this'). Error `already_exists` if the same video was processed before. Bluesky-hosted accounts need a verified email. Poll until state COMPLETED and blob present, then createRecord with app.bsky.embed.video.

endpoints.response_shape: {"jobStatus":{jobId, did, state, progress?, blob?, error?, message?}}
endpoints.notes: Needs a service-auth token with lxm=app.bsky.video.getJobStatus (lexicon-defined lxm) per community sources; the official tutorial's agent handles this.

endpoints.purpose: Link-card metadata (undocumented helper used by the official app)
endpoints.response_shape: {url, title, description, image (often a proxied cardyb.bsky.app/v1/image?... URL), error?}
endpoints.notes: Unofficial/undocumented endpoint; the protocol has NO server-side unfurl - the client must build app.bsky.embed.external itself (fetch OG tags yourself or via cardyb), download the thumb, uploadBlob it (<=1,000,000 bytes), then reference it.

official_api.free_tier: Entire API is free and unmetered apart from rate limits (valid 2026-10-07). No API keys, no developer account, no app registration. Per-account rate limits from docs (bsky-docs rate-limits.md): 3,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP; repo writes 5,000 points/hour and 35,000 points/day where CREATE=3, UPDATE=2, DELETE=1 (about 1,666 new records/hour, 11,666/day); createSession 30 per 5 min / 300 per day; updateHandle 10 per 5 min / 50 per day. Video: 25 videos or 10 GB per day (Sept 2024 figure, subject to change; query getUploadLimits).
official_api.paid_tiers: None. No paid API tiers exist.
official_api.rate_limits: Headers returned: ratelimit-limit, ratelimit-remaining, ratelimit-reset (unix seconds), ratelimit-policy (e.g. '30;w=300'); HTTP 429 with error 'RateLimitExceeded' when exceeded. Numbers as in free_tier.
official_api.media_upload_flow: Images: uploadBlob (raw bytes, Content-Type = mime) -> reference returned blob object in app.bsky.embed.images (max 4, each <= 2,000,000 bytes, image/*; supply alt + aspectRatio; official app re-encodes to JPEG <= 2000px historically, now up to 4000px). Link-card thumb: same uploadBlob, <= 1,000,000 bytes. Video: getServiceAuth (aud=did:web:<PDS host>, lxm=com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob) -> POST https://video.bsky.app/xrpc/app.bsky.video.uploadVideo?did=&name= with Bearer service token and video/mp4 body -> poll getJobStatus until blob -> createRecord with app.bsky.embed.video. New in 2026: app.bsky.embed.gallery (mixed media; schema max 20 items, clients told to enforce a soft limit of 10 in authoring UIs).
official_api.server_side_scheduling: None. Posts are created immediately; createdAt is client-supplied (ISO 8601 with Z). Scheduling must be done locally (the device must be on and online at send time).
official_api.token_lifetime_and_refresh: OAuth public client: access token < 30 min (typically 5-15), refresh tokens single-use and rotated on every refresh, total session max 2 weeks then re-authorize. Legacy createSession: accessJwt short-lived (official docs only say 'expires after a few minutes'; community observes ~1-2 hours), refreshJwt long-lived (community: weeks to ~90 days, unverified); refresh via refreshSession with Bearer refreshJwt; no hard session cap as long as you keep refreshing.
official_api.app_review_required: No. No app review, registration, or approval of any kind. For OAuth the only 'registration' is publishing the client-metadata JSON at an https URL.
official_api.unreviewed_app_restrictions: None - every app is 'unreviewed'. Full posting, media and thread capability from day one on a personal account. The only differences come from client type: public clients (all local-first apps) get 2-week OAuth sessions; the http://localhost loopback client is labelled a development mechanism and shows a generic/unverified client on the consent screen (exact wording unverified).
official_api.account_requirements: Any ordinary Bluesky account (free, no business/professional account concept). Video upload on Bluesky-hosted accounts requires a verified email. App passwords require the user to create one in Settings > App passwords (do not enable 'privileged' unless DMs are needed). Developer Guidelines (docs/support/developer-guidelines) forbid spam/automated bulk interactions and automated follower generation; cross-posting a user's own posts is fine.

handoff.web_intent_params: text=<URL-encoded text, newlines as %0A> (only parameter; 300 grapheme limit still applies; user must confirm in the composer; unauthenticated users are prompted to sign in first). Example from docs: https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=I%27m%20reading%20through%20the%20Bluesky%20API%20docs%21%20%F0%9F%A6%8B%0Ahttps%3A//docs.bsky.app
handoff.android_share: Official app package xyz.blueskyweb.app. Its main activity registers android.intent.action.SEND for text/plain, image/* and video/*, and android.intent.action.SEND_MULTIPLE for image/* (category DEFAULT) - verified in social-app plugins/shareExtension/withIntentFilters.js. So NEFORUM can fire ACTION_SEND with EXTRA_TEXT and/or EXTRA_STREAM (content:// URIs with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION) targeted at package xyz.blueskyweb.app; the module converts it to bluesky://intent/compose?text=...&imageUris=...|videoUri=... internally. Module README says up to 4 images for multi-image share (may be stale now that posts can hold more via gallery). The https://bsky.app host is an auto-verified App Link, so opening https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=... also lands in the app; deep-link scheme bluesky://intent/compose?text=... works too.
handoff.ios_share: Bundle id xyz.blueskyweb.app; URL scheme `bluesky` -> bluesky://intent/compose?text=<encoded>. Universal links: applinks:bsky.app, so https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text= opens the app. Share extension target 'Share-with-Bluesky' (xyz.blueskyweb.app.Share-with-Bluesky) with NSExtensionActivationRule: text supported, web URL max 1, images max 10, movie max 1 - so a UIActivityViewController share sheet with text + up to 10 images or 1 video can prefill the Bluesky composer (user picks Bluesky in the sheet; cannot be targeted programmatically).
handoff.desktop: Open https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=<encoded> in the default browser (web app composer; user attaches media manually). Windows/macOS have no official native Bluesky desktop client; the web app is a PWA.
handoff.notes: Text-only via URL on every platform; media prefill only through the OS share sheet (Android ACTION_SEND / iOS share extension), never via the intent URL. The compose intent cannot pre-set reply targets, link cards or languages.

text_limits.counting_rule: 300 Unicode extended grapheme clusters (lexicon maxGraphemes 300) AND at most 3,000 UTF-8 bytes (maxLength 3000). Every grapheme counts 1 regardless of width; an emoji ZWJ sequence or flag counts as 1 grapheme. URLs are NOT shortened by the server - the full URL text counts (the official client shows a truncated display text in `text` and puts the full URL in a link facet, which is the trick to save characters). Facet byteStart/byteEnd are zero-indexed UTF-8 byte offsets (end exclusive) - compute on the UTF-8 bytes, not Dart String code units (UTF-16).
text_limits.notes: Hashtags are plain text plus an app.bsky.richtext.facet#tag facet (tag stored without '#', max 64 graphemes / 640 bytes); the post-level `tags` array (max 8, same per-item limits) is separate hidden metadata. Mentions: facet#mention with the resolved DID. Links: facet#link with full uri. langs: max 3 BCP-47 codes. Alt text: no schema limit on images (official UI caps at 2000 chars - unverified). Grapheme counting in Dart: use the `characters` package (`text.characters.length`); the community `bluesky_text` package does counting and facet extraction.

media_limits.image_formats: accept image/* at the lexicon level; the official apps/AppView serve JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF (static). Official client re-encodes to JPEG (now up to 4000px long edge). Link-card thumb max 1,000,000 bytes. New app.bsky.embed.gallery allows mixed media, soft limit 10 items (schema 20).
media_limits.video: 1 video per post (app.bsky.embed.video), video/mp4 only at the lexicon (maxSize 300,000,000 bytes). Announced limits: up to 10 minutes and 300 MB (Aug 2026; was 3 min from Jan 2026, 60 s at Sept 2024 launch). Processed asynchronously by video.bsky.app (transcode to HLS); captions up to 20 WebVTT files of <= 20,000 bytes each. Daily quota: 25 videos / 10 GB per account (Sept 2024 figure; check getUploadLimits). Video cannot be combined with images in one post.
media_limits.aspect_ratio: Any; supply aspectRatio {width,height} on each image/video so clients lay out correctly. Image grid historically cropped; since the April 2026 carousel update mixed aspect ratios display uncropped.

gotchas: docs.bsky.app URLs now 308-redirect to bsky.network/docs and endpoints.bsky.app (JS-rendered); read the markdown sources in github.com/bluesky-social/bsky-docs or the lexicon JSON in bluesky-social/atproto instead.

OAuth is unusually heavy: PAR + PKCE S256 + DPoP (ES256 keypair per session, server nonce retry on 400 use_dpop_nonce / 401) + hosted client-metadata JSON. Do not hand-roll; use pub.dev `atproto_oauth`/`atproto` (atprotodart.com, active in 2026) which handle DPoP and refresh.

Public OAuth clients get at most a 2-week session; the user must re-login every 14 days. App passwords avoid this (refresh indefinitely) but are discouraged for end-user apps and give broad access. Offer both: OAuth default, app-password fallback.

A hosted https client_id cannot use http://127.0.0.1 redirects; native apps must use a reverse-domain custom scheme matching the client_id hostname (e.g. client_id https://neforum.example.org/oauth/client-metadata.json -> org.example.neforum:/callback) or https same-origin App/Universal Links. On Windows/macOS that means registering a custom URL scheme for the desktop app. The loopback alternative requires client_id literally `http://localhost?...` which the official tutorials call development-only.
Mobile custom-scheme redirects are not restricted to the app that claims them (any app can register the scheme); the spec accepts this for native public clients, PKCE protects the code.
Refresh tokens are single-use. Persist the new pair atomically and serialize refreshes across isolates/tabs or you will invalidate your own session.
Facet offsets are UTF-8 bytes; Dart strings are UTF-16. Convert with utf8.encode before computing byteStart/byteEnd. Grapheme count via `characters` package, not .length.
Server does not auto-detect links, mentions or hashtags - without facets they are plain text. Mentions require resolving @handle -> DID (resolveHandle) at compose time.

No server-side link unfurl: to get a link card you must build app.bsky.embed.external yourself (fetch OG/title/description, download thumb <= 1,000,000 bytes, uploadBlob it). The official app uses the undocumented https://cardyb.bsky.app/v1/extract?url= service.
Exactly one embed per post: images OR video OR link card OR quote (quote+media via recordWithMedia). A post with 4 images cannot also carry a link card.
Image limit changed in 2026 from 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 bytes (post images only); link-card thumbs are still 1,000,000. Old third-party docs still say 1 MB.
Blobs are garbage-collected if not referenced by a record within minutes - upload immediately before createRecord, not at draft time.

Video is not uploaded to the PDS: it goes to https://video.bsky.app with a getServiceAuth token whose aud is did:web:<PDS host> and lxm=com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob, with ?did=&name= query params and Content-Type video/mp4, then poll getJobStatus. Requires verified email on bsky.social accounts. Only mp4 at the lexicon level; re-encode mov/webm client-side.
Threads: root/parent strong refs need both uri AND cid from each createRecord response; root stays the first post for all later posts.
Rate limits are points-based: 3 points per create, 5,000/hour and 35,000/day; a 429 returns RateLimitExceeded with ratelimit-reset (unix seconds).

Self-hosted PDS users: never hard-code bsky.social; resolve handle -> DID (plc.directory or did:web) -> service #atproto_pds -> serviceEndpoint and verify handle bidirectionally. Entryway for bsky.social accounts is https://bsky.social even though the actual PDS host is like https://puffball.us-east.host.bsky.network.
createdAt is client-supplied; a far-future timestamp is accepted but feeds may hide/sort it oddly - always use now in UTC with 'Z'.
The compose intent URL cannot prefill media; media only via OS share sheet (Android ACTION_SEND/SEND_MULTIPLE to xyz.blueskyweb.app; iOS share extension accepts text, 1 URL, 10 images or 1 movie).
Email 2FA on the main password returns AuthFactorTokenRequired; app passwords are the normal way to avoid this in third-party clients (behaviour with 2FA accounts unverified).
unverified_claims: Legacy accessJwt lifetime (~1-2 hours) and refreshJwt lifetime (~90 days / '2 months') - official docs only say 'a few minutes' and 'lasts longer'.

App passwords bypass email 2FA and cannot delete/migrate the account or change email; 'privileged' app passwords are needed for chat.bsky DMs - from community/help sources, not read on an official page.

Video daily quota of 25 videos / 10 GB is the Sept 2024 launch number; current quota not confirmed (use getUploadLimits). The 10-minute/300 MB limit comes from Engadget (2026-08-26) and lexicon maxSize, not a page on bsky.social.
Image limit raised from 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 bytes in April 2026 (TechCrunch via search summary); the 2,000,000 value itself is verified in the current lexicon.

Exact rpc: scope string required for getServiceAuth/video upload under granular OAuth scopes (likely rpc:com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob?aud=did:web:<pds> or rpc:*?aud=*); and that bsky.social already enforces granular scopes while still accepting transition:generic.
What the bsky.social consent screen displays for an http://localhost loopback client, and whether Bluesky will keep allowing it indefinitely for shipped desktop apps.

Video job states names (JOB_STATE_CREATED/ENCODING/SCANNING/COMPLETED/FAILED) and that getJobStatus/getUploadLimits need service-auth tokens with their own lxm - recalled from app.bsky.video.defs and community PHP docs, not re-read.
cardyb.bsky.app/v1/extract response shape and that it is tolerated for third-party use (it is undocumented).
Official app's image re-encode behaviour (JPEG, EXIF stripped, 4000px) and alt-text UI cap of 2000 chars.
Android share module 'up to 4 images' may be outdated after the 2026 gallery/carousel change; iOS extension max 10 images is verified from Info.plist.
Android ACTION_SEND filters are on the first <activity> (MainActivity) of xyz.blueskyweb.app - inferred from the plugin code, not from a built manifest.
The bsky.social AppView/CDN serves GIF/WebP/PNG/JPEG; animated GIFs are posted via external embed (tenor) not image blobs.

web_session.how: Technically possible: load https://bsky.app in a WebView (webview_flutter / flutter_inappwebview), let the user log in, then either drive the composer DOM or, more sensibly, read the session from localStorage (the web app stores the atproto session JSON, including accessJwt/refreshJwt or DPoP OAuth state) and call the XRPC API directly. But it is pointless: the web client is open source and uses exactly the same public, free, unauthenticated-registration API described above, so the direct API path is strictly simpler and more robust.
web_session.risk: Low to negligible from Bluesky's side: third-party clients are explicitly contemplated by the Developer Guidelines; there is no ToS clause against alternative clients or automation of your own posts; enforcement targets spam/bulk interactions. Practical risks are breakage when the web UI changes, lack of 2FA/OAuth consent transparency, and storing the user's full-session tokens outside the official app. Not recommended - use the API.
